examples.en: That player is the biggest contributor to the victory.

examples.ko: 건국 공신들은 나라에서 큰 상을 받았어요.
examples.en: The founding heroes received great rewards from the country.

examples.ko: 이번 프로젝트 성공의 공신은 바로 우리 팀장님이에요.
examples.en: The one who made this project a success is our team leader.

examples.ko: 그를 승리의 공신으로 칭찬하는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people praise him as the key to the victory.
I felt hurt because I wasn't treated like a key contributor.

examples.ko: 신입 사원이 매출 상승의 공신이 됐어요.
examples.en: The new employee became the reason sales went up.

explain: 원래는 나라에 큰 공을 세운 사람을 가리켰어요. 지금은 '일등 공신'처럼 어떤 일이 잘되게 한 사람이나 원인을 가볍게 말할 때도 많이 써요. 같은 소리의 '공신(공부의 신)'이라는 신조어와는 달라요.
explain_en: It originally referred to someone who rendered great service to the nation. Today it is also used lightly, as in '일등 공신', for a person or cause that made something succeed. It is different from the slang '공신' meaning a study genius.

examples.en: It hurt that his family treated him coldly.
If you treat customers coldly, the shop's reputation gets worse.

examples.ko: 새로 온 직원을 냉대하는 분위기가 싫어요.
examples.en: I dislike the atmosphere of giving the new employee the cold shoulder.
That person treated me far too coldly.
I felt my relatives were cold to me, so I stopped visiting.

examples.ko: 이웃이 냉대해도 저는 늘 먼저 인사해요.
examples.en: Even if the neighbors are cold to me, I always greet them first.

explain: 사람을 차갑고 무심하게 대할 때 써요. 반대말은 '환대하다'이고, 비슷한 말로 '푸대접하다'가 있어요. 받는 쪽에서는 '냉대를 받다'라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It is used when you treat someone in a cold, careless way. The opposite is '환대하다' and a similar word is '푸대접하다'. From the receiver's side you can also say '냉대를 받다'.

examples.ko: 요즘 동생은 공부와 담쌓고 게임만 해요.
examples.en: These days my brother has given up on studying and only plays games.

examples.ko: 친구와 담쌓은 지 벌써 일 년이 됐어요.
examples.en: It has already been a year since I cut ties with my friend.
Shutting each other out won't solve the problem.
Why do you live cut off from your family?

examples.ko: 책과 담쌓았던 아이가 이제는 도서관에 가요.
examples.en: The kid who used to want nothing to do with books now goes to the library.
Once you cut someone off, it's hard to get close again.

explain: '~와 담쌓다'는 어떤 사람이나 일과 관계를 끊거나 아예 가까이하지 않는다는 비유로 써요. 실제로 담을 만드는 뜻일 때는 '담을 쌓다'처럼 띄어 써요. '공부랑 담쌓았다'는 말은 공부를 안 한다는 뜻으로 일상에서 자주 해요.
explain_en: '~와 담쌓다' is a figurative expression meaning to cut ties with a person or to stay away from something entirely. When you literally build a wall, it is written separately as '담을 쌓다'. People often say '공부랑 담쌓았다' in daily life to mean someone doesn't study at all.

en: insult; desecration (of someone's dignity or beliefs)

examples.ko: 그 말은 우리 모두에 대한 모독이에요.
examples.en: Those words are an insult to all of us.
Criticism came out that it was an affront to religion.
That question felt like an insult to me.

examples.ko: 선생님은 학생들 앞에서 모독을 당했다고 느꼈어요.
examples.en: The teacher felt humiliated in front of the students.
The person who made the insulting remark apologized.
That kind of behavior is close to an outrage.

explain: '모욕'은 사람에게 창피를 주는 것이고, '모독'은 존엄, 신념, 죽은 사람, 종교처럼 소중한 것을 더럽히는 무거운 말이에요. '~에 대한 모독'이라고 자주 써요. 가벼운 말다툼에는 어울리지 않아요.
explain_en: '모욕' is shaming a person, while '모독' is a heavy word for defiling something precious, such as dignity, beliefs, the dead, or religion. It is often used as '~에 대한 모독'. It doesn't suit a light quarrel.

en: to be heartless; to be unsympathetic; to be cold-hearted

examples.en: Turning away from a neighbor in need is so heartless.
Please don't speak so coldly.
The employees are having a hard time because of their cold-hearted boss.

examples.ko: 아이를 혼자 두고 가다니 몰인정하지 않아요?
examples.en: Isn't it heartless to leave a child alone and go?
If I seemed heartless, I'm sorry.

examples.ko: 몰인정하기로 소문난 가게 주인이 오늘은 웃었어요.
examples.en: The shop owner, known for being cold-hearted, smiled today.

explain: 인정이나 동정심이 없어서 남의 어려움을 모른 척하는 사람이나 행동에 써요. 일상에서는 '매정하다', '냉정하다'를 더 자주 말해요. 반대는 '인정이 많다', '정이 많다'예요.
explain_en: It describes a person or action that has no compassion and ignores other people's troubles. In daily speech '매정하다' and '냉정하다' are more common. The opposite is '인정이 많다' or '정이 많다'.

en: to be peaceful; to be tranquil

examples.en: The exam is tomorrow, but my younger sibling is carefree.
If you stay so carefree like that, you'll be late.

examples.ko: 무사태평한 성격이라서 걱정을 잘 안 해요.
examples.en: I have an easygoing personality, so I rarely worry.
Even though it's a crisis, he's wearing a carefree look.
My father always laughs in a carefree way.

examples.ko: 이런 상황에서 어떻게 무사태평할 수 있어요?
examples.en: How can you be so carefree in a situation like this?

explain: 걱정해야 할 상황인데도 아무 걱정이 없어 보일 때 써요. 놀리거나 나무라는 말투로 쓰는 일이 많아요. 좋은 뜻으로 편안하게 말하고 싶으면 '느긋하다'를 써요.
explain_en: Use it when someone looks worry-free even though the situation calls for concern. It is often said in a teasing or scolding tone. For a positive, relaxed tone, say '느긋하다' instead.

examples.en: A shop that treats its customers coldly doesn't last long.

examples.ko: 그분은 찾아온 친척을 박대하지 않고 따뜻하게 맞아 줬어요.
examples.en: She didn't turn away her visiting relative and welcomed them warmly.
If you treat newcomers badly, the team atmosphere gets worse.
You shouldn't treat someone badly just because they're a stranger.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 부모님을 박대했다가 나중에 크게 후회했어요.
examples.en: He treated his parents coldly and later regretted it deeply.

examples.ko: 어려울 때 도와준 친구를 박대할 수는 없어요.
examples.en: I can't treat a friend who helped me in hard times badly.

explain: 손님이나 찾아온 사람, 도움을 준 사람을 소홀하고 야박하게 대할 때 써요. 반대는 정성껏 맞이하는 '환대하다'예요. 대화에서는 '푸대접하다'나 '함부로 대하다'라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It is used when someone treats a guest, a visitor or a person who helped them in a neglectful, stingy way. The opposite is '환대하다' (to welcome warmly). In conversation people also say '푸대접하다' or '함부로 대하다'.

en: to be betrayed; to be stabbed in the back

examples.en: I'm hurt because a friend I trusted betrayed me.

examples.ko: 동업자에게 배신당한 뒤로 사람을 잘 못 믿어요.
examples.en: Since my business partner betrayed me, I can't trust people easily.
Anyone gets angry when they are betrayed.
He felt that his family had betrayed him.
I couldn't share my true feelings for fear of being betrayed.

examples.ko: 또 배신당하고 싶지 않아서 거리를 뒀어요.
examples.en: I didn't want to be betrayed again, so I kept my distance.

explain: '배신하다'를 당한 쪽에서 말하는 형태예요. 믿음을 깬 사람은 '배신하다', 상처 입은 사람은 '배신당하다'를 써요. '뒤통수를 맞다'라는 생생한 표현도 있어요. 연인이나 친구 사이의 큰 감정이 담겨 있어서 가벼운 일에는 안 써요.
explain_en: This is the form you use from the side of the person who was betrayed. The one who broke the trust does 배신하다, and the one who was hurt is 배신당하다. There is also the vivid expression 뒤통수를 맞다 (get stabbed in the back). It carries strong feelings, so it is not used for minor things.

examples.en: The children are running around playing soldiers.
Toy soldiers are standing in a row.
My younger brother stood stiffly like a soldier.

examples.ko: 그 가게 입구에는 병정 인형이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a toy soldier doll at the entrance of that shop.
The scene of little soldiers marching was impressive.

examples.ko: 아버지는 어릴 때 병정 흉내를 자주 내셨다고 해요.
examples.en: My father says he often pretended to be a soldier when he was little.

explain: 요즘 군인은 '군인'이나 '군인 아저씨'라고 하고, '병정'은 옛날 말투이거나 '병정놀이', '장난감 병정'처럼 아이들 놀이와 함께 많이 들어요. 어른을 진지하게 가리킬 때는 잘 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: Today people say '군인' for a soldier; '병정' sounds old-fashioned or shows up with children's play, as in '병정놀이' and '장난감 병정'. It isn't normally used to refer seriously to an adult soldier.

en: to retaliate; to take revenge; to hit back

examples.en: He took revenge on the friend who teased him.

examples.ko: 보복하려고 일부러 약속을 어긴 건 아니에요.
examples.en: I didn't break the promise on purpose to get back at him.

examples.ko: 상대 팀에게 보복하는 대신 경기에 집중했어요.
examples.en: Instead of retaliating against the other team, they focused on the game.
You must not retaliate just because someone reported you.

examples.ko: 보복할 기회를 기다리는 사람은 마음이 편하지 않아요.
examples.en: Someone waiting for a chance to get even is not at peace.

examples.ko: 보복하고 싶은 마음을 참은 게 잘한 일이에요.
examples.en: Holding back the urge to retaliate was the right thing.

explain: 보복하다는 복수하다와 비슷하지만 '보복 운전', '보복 범죄', '보복 관세'처럼 한 덩어리 말로도 많이 나와요. 대개 나쁜 행동에 나쁜 행동으로 되갚는다는 뜻이라 부정적인 느낌이 강해요. 신고한 사람에게 보복하는 일은 뉴스에서도 자주 다뤄요.
explain_en: 보복하다 is close to 복수하다, but it also appears a lot in set phrases such as 보복 운전 (road rage), 보복 범죄 and 보복 관세 (retaliatory tariff). It usually means paying back a bad act with another, so the feel is strongly negative. Retaliating against someone who reported you is a common news topic.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 저와 생판 모르는 사이예요.
examples.en: That person and I are complete strangers.

examples.ko: 생판 처음 보는 사람이 길을 물어서 알려 줬어요.
examples.en: A total stranger asked me for directions, so I told him.

examples.ko: 이사 간 동네가 생판 낯설어서 길을 자꾸 잃어요.
examples.en: The neighborhood I moved to is totally unfamiliar, so I keep getting lost.

examples.ko: 생판 다른 이야기를 하길래 제가 잘못 들은 줄 알았어요.
examples.en: He started talking about something completely different, so I thought I had misheard.

examples.ko: 생판 남인데 왜 그 사람이 우리 일에 끼어들어요?
examples.en: He is a complete outsider, so why is he butting into our business?

examples.ko: 이 노래는 생판 처음 들어 보는 곡이에요.
examples.en: This is a song I am hearing for the very first time.

explain: 뒤에 '모르다', '낯설다', '다르다', '남' 같은 말이 와서 '전혀', '완전히'의 뜻을 강하게 해 줘요. '전혀'는 보통 부정 표현과 함께 쓰지만, '생판'은 '생판 다르다'처럼 긍정 표현에도 쓰고 입말 느낌이 강해요.
explain_en: It goes with words like '모르다', '낯설다', '다르다' and '남' to strengthen the sense of 'completely'. '전혀' usually pairs with negatives, but '생판' also works with affirmative phrases like '생판 다르다', and it sounds colloquial.

examples.ko: 두 팀은 오랜 숙적이라서 경기마다 치열해요.
examples.en: The two teams are old rivals, so every match is fierce.
We met our longtime rival in the final.

examples.ko: 그 둘은 학교 다닐 때부터 숙적 사이였어요.
examples.en: Those two have been rivals since their school days.
After beating my old rival, tears came out.
The hero of the comic faces his arch-enemy at the end.
This year we got a chance to get revenge on our old rival.

explain: 오래전부터 맞서 온 상대를 말하고, 스포츠 뉴스나 만화, 영화에서 자주 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 가벼운 경쟁 상대를 '라이벌'이라고 하는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: It means an opponent you have been up against for a long time, and appears often in sports news, comics and movies. In daily talk, people often say '라이벌' for a lighter kind of competitor.

examples.en: Don't pour curses on someone you broke up with.

examples.ko: 그는 아무 이유 없이 나에게 악담을 했어요.
examples.en: He said hateful things to me for no reason.

examples.ko: 악담을 들으면 하루 종일 기분이 안 좋아요.
examples.en: When I hear hateful words, I feel bad all day.

examples.ko: 그 사람의 악담에 상처를 많이 받았어요.
examples.en: I was badly hurt by his hateful words.
There are too many hateful remarks in online comments.

examples.ko: 악담 대신 따뜻한 말 한마디를 해 주세요.
examples.en: Say a warm word instead of hateful ones.

explain: 남이 잘못되기를 바라며 하는 모진 말이에요. '험담'은 남의 흠을 흉보는 말이고, '악담'은 상대가 안 좋게 되길 바라는 말이라는 느낌이 더 강해요. '악담을 하다', '악담을 퍼붓다'로 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It means harsh words said wishing someone ill. '험담' is speaking badly about someone's faults, while '악담' feels more like wishing harm on them. It often appears as '악담을 하다' or '악담을 퍼붓다'.

en: to disdain; to belittle; to underestimate

examples.en: You shouldn't look down on someone just because they're young.
He never looked down on poor people.

examples.ko: 사람들이 그를 업신여겼지만 그는 끝까지 노력했어요.
examples.en: People belittled him, but he kept trying to the end.
You need to fix your attitude of looking down on your friends.

examples.ko: 외국인이라고 업신여겨서 그 점원에게 화가 났어요.
examples.en: I got angry at that clerk for looking down on me because I'm a foreigner.
We underestimated the other team and lost badly.

explain: 상대를 낮게 보고 하찮게 대한다는 뜻이라, 무시하는 태도가 말이나 행동으로 드러나는 장면에 어울려요. '깔보다'는 더 구어체이고, '무시하다'는 관심을 두지 않는 경우에도 써요. 당하는 쪽에서는 '업신여김을 받다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It means treating someone as lowly or worthless, and fits scenes where contempt shows in words or actions. '깔보다' is more colloquial, and '무시하다' can also mean simply ignoring something. From the receiving side you say '업신여김을 받다'.

examples.en: That mistake is not easily forgiven.

examples.ko: 거짓말은 어떤 이유로도 용서될 수 없어요.
examples.en: A lie can't be forgiven for any reason.
Because I apologized sincerely, everything was forgiven.
Since he was a child, the mood was that it could be forgiven this time.
I thought breaking the promise had been forgiven.

examples.ko: 사정을 알고 나니 그의 행동이 용서돼요.
examples.en: Now that I know the circumstances, his behavior seems forgivable.

explain: '용서되다'는 '용서가 된다'는 느낌이라 보통 '용서되지 않다', '용서될 수 없다'처럼 부정으로 많이 써요. 내가 누군가를 용서할 때는 '용서하다' 또는 '봐주다'가 자연스러워요.
explain_en: '용서되다' is mostly used in the negative, like '용서되지 않다' or '용서될 수 없다'. When you yourself forgive someone, '용서하다' or the casual '봐주다' sounds more natural.

examples.ko: 두 나라는 우호 관계를 이어 왔어요.
examples.en: The two countries have kept up friendly relations.
A delegation visited to strengthen friendly ties.
They held talks with a neighboring country in a friendly atmosphere.
A new friendship agreement was signed.
That team is very friendly toward us.
The citizens welcomed the visitors warmly.

explain: 나라나 단체 사이에서 사이좋게 지내는 관계에 자주 쓰고, 개인 사이에는 '친하다', '친구' 같은 말을 써요. '우호 관계'처럼 붙여 쓰고 '우호적이다', '우호적으로'로 활용해요. 반대는 '적대'예요.
explain_en: It is mainly for good relations between countries or organizations; between individuals people say '친하다' or '친구'. It appears as '우호 관계' and takes forms like '우호적이다' and '우호적으로'. The opposite is '적대'.

examples.en: My parents keep urging me to get a job.

examples.ko: 회사가 직원에게 사직을 종용했다는 기사를 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw an article saying the company pressured an employee to resign.
A senior kept pushing me to join the club, which felt burdensome.

examples.ko: 누가 종용한 것도 아닌데 스스로 나섰어요.
examples.en: Nobody pushed him, yet he stepped forward on his own.
I disliked the atmosphere that pressed me to apologize.
The doctor didn't press me to have the surgery.

explain: '권하다'는 중립적이지만, 종용하다는 상대가 원하지 않는 일을 계속 권해서 부담을 주는 느낌이에요. 주로 사직, 사과, 결혼처럼 무거운 일에 쓰고 뉴스에서도 자주 나와요.
explain_en: '권하다' is neutral, but 종용하다 feels like repeatedly pushing someone toward something they don't want, which puts pressure on them. It is used for weighty matters like resignation, apology or marriage, and appears often in the news.

examples.ko: 회사 안에 파벌이 생겨서 분위기가 안 좋아요.
examples.en: Cliques formed inside the company, so the atmosphere is bad.

examples.ko: 그는 파벌 싸움에 휘말리기 싫어서 퇴사했어요.
examples.en: He quit because he didn't want to get caught up in factional fights.

examples.ko: 정당 안의 파벌 때문에 결정이 늦어졌어요.
examples.en: The decision was delayed because of factions within the party.

examples.ko: 특정 파벌에만 줄을 서면 오래가기 어려워요.
examples.en: If you side only with one faction, it's hard to last long.

examples.ko: 이 팀은 파벌 없이 모두가 사이좋게 일해요.
examples.en: On this team, everyone works well together without cliques.

examples.ko: 파벌을 만들지 말고 서로 도와야 해요.
examples.en: We shouldn't form cliques; we should help each other.

explain: '패거리'보다 점잖은 말이고, 정당이나 회사, 학교 같은 조직 안에서 이익을 위해 뭉친 무리에 써요. '파벌 싸움', '파벌을 만들다'처럼 쓰고 대체로 부정적이에요.
explain_en: It is more polite than '패거리' (gang) and is used for groups within a party, company or school that band together for their own interests. It appears in '파벌 싸움' and '파벌을 만들다' and is generally negative.

examples.ko: 선생님의 편애 때문에 반 분위기가 안 좋아요.
examples.en: The class atmosphere is bad because of the teacher's favoritism.

examples.ko: 부모의 편애는 아이들 사이를 멀어지게 해요.
examples.en: Parents' favoritism drives their children apart.

examples.ko: 저는 형만 챙기는 아버지의 편애가 서운했어요.
examples.en: I felt hurt by my father's favoritism, since he only looked after my brother.

examples.ko: 편애 없이 모두에게 공평한 선생님이 되고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to be a teacher who treats everyone fairly, without favoritism.

examples.ko: 막내를 향한 편애가 심하다는 이야기를 자주 들어요.
examples.en: I often hear that the favoritism toward the youngest is severe.
He grew up as his mother's favorite.

explain: 특정 사람만 더 아끼고 챙기는 마음과 행동이에요. 반의어는 '공평'이고, 집단을 가르는 '차별'과 달리 가족·학교처럼 가까운 사이에서 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It is caring for and looking after one particular person more than others. The opposite idea is '공평' (fairness), and unlike '차별', which splits groups apart, it is often said about close settings such as family and school.
